passage:
Dear Jahnavi,

Thank you for your note after Thursday's client pitch. You said my smile at the start settled the room, and I want to answer honestly. It's true I smile broadly as I walk into a room. That kind of smile is best when I really feel welcoming, and Thursday I did. But last month, when I was worried about the budget cuts, I smiled just as widely, and afterwards my jaw ached and I felt hollow. I'm learning to tell the difference. Now I take one breath before a meeting and ask myself what I actually feel. If it's worry, I keep the smile smaller and say so to a colleague later.

Thanks for noticing.

Akash

qa.q: On which day was the client pitch?
qa.a: The client pitch was on Thursday.

qa.q: What does Akash feel about smiling broadly when worried, and what shows it?
qa.a: Akash feels hollow and worn down by it, shown by the aching jaw after smiling widely over budget worries.

qa.q: What could Akash do to keep that smile honest?
qa.a: Akash could take a breath before meetings, check the real feeling underneath and share worries with a colleague.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi have seen Akash's smile?
qa.a: Jahnavi saw it as settling the room, and Jahnavi likely did not know about the worry on the other days.

grounding: Akash uses a broad smile to open meetings, which works with honest goodwill and wears Akash down when over worry.

passage: I'm Harish, and I run a small travel agency. When customers walk in, my first move is a big, open smile. I've been told it's my best marketing. And most days it's real: I enjoy people, and I love sending someone to the mountains for the first time. But there was a month last year when I was behind on rent and every time the door opened I put the smile on like a jacket. My friend Ojas, who works next door, said, "You look tired, yaar." I said I was fine. He said, "Your smile's fine. It's your eyes." That night I told my wife about the rent. Now I keep the smile for the moments I mean it, and I let myself look serious when I'm worried.

qa.q: What kind of business does Harish run?
qa.a: Harish runs a small travel agency.

qa.q: What was Harish feeling under the smile during the bad month, and how did Ojas notice?
qa.a: Harish was worried about rent and tired, and Ojas noticed it in Harish's eyes though the smile looked fine.

qa.q: What could Harish do to handle worry without being worn out?
qa.a: Harish could talk to someone trusted, as Harish did at home that night, and allow a serious face when worried.

qa.q: How might customers see Harish's smile on a day when Harish is worried?
qa.a: They would likely read it as warmth, since they can't see the worry, which is why it matters that Harish can be honest elsewhere.

grounding: Harish uses a broad smile with customers, honest when he means it and draining when covering worry.

subtype: Broad smile as customer or leadership tool [Regulating]
passage: I'm Kamal, and I've worked with Zainab for two years at the startup in Hyderabad. She's twenty-six, our youngest team lead, and she opens every Monday meeting with a huge smile, arms wide: "Good morning, superstars!" It works. People sit up, laugh, relax. Clients love it too. But over the last month, I noticed something. When the news of layoffs started going round, her smile stayed the same size, but her eyes didn't match it. After the meeting, she'd go straight to her cabin and shut the door. Once I saw her through the glass, face in her hands. I don't know exactly what she was feeling. Maybe worry about her team. Maybe her own job. Last Friday I knocked and said, "You don't have to smile for me." She laughed, tiredly. "Is it that obvious?" Then she told me she'd been sleeping four hours a night. We talked for an hour. On Monday her smile was smaller, and more real.

qa.q: How does Zainab open every Monday meeting?
qa.a: With a huge smile, arms wide: "Good morning, superstars!"

qa.q: What might Zainab have been feeling during the layoff rumours?
qa.a: She seemed worried and exhausted behind her broad smile, perhaps about her team or her own job, and was sleeping only four hours.

qa.q: What did Kamal do that helped?
qa.a: Kamal knocked and gently told her she didn't have to smile for him, which let her talk honestly.

qa.q: How did the team experience Zainab's broad smile?
qa.a: It helped them sit up, laugh and relax at the start of meetings, as it did for clients.

grounding: Shows through an observer a young team lead using a broad smile to set people at ease while habitual smiling over worry wears her down.

passage:
Week one. Kunal, twenty-four, started as a sales executive at a car showroom in Jaipur. His mentor Aparna told him, "Smile big when customers walk in. It opens doors." So he did, all day, even when a customer was rude, even when he was worried about his monthly target. By Friday his cheeks ached, and a customer asked, "Why are you grinning like that?"
Week two. Kunal told Aparna he felt fake. She watched him greet a family and said, "Your smile is big, but it's the same for everyone. Try meaning it. Look at who's in front of you." With the next customer, an old man with a walking stick, Kunal smiled because he actually liked the man's hat. The man smiled back.
Week four. Kunal still smiled broadly at the door. But on a tough day he told Aparna he was stressed about the target, instead of grinning through it. She helped him plan his calls.

qa.q: What did the customer ask Kunal at the end of week one?
qa.a: "Why are you grinning like that?"

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling by the end of week one?
qa.a: He felt tired and fake, his cheeks aching from forced smiling while he worried about his target.

qa.q: What did Aparna advise that made the smile work better?
qa.a: To mean the smile by paying attention to the person in front of him, instead of the same big grin for everyone.

qa.q: How did the old man react to Kunal's genuine smile?
qa.a: He smiled back, suggesting the honest warmth reached him.

grounding: Shows a young professional learning that a broad smile works best when it matches real goodwill, and that smiling over worry is draining.

subtype: Broad smile as customer or leadership tool [Regulating]
passage: Noor, you've just been made front-office manager, so let your Tarun sir tell you something. At twenty-four, I was the youngest duty manager at a big hotel in Goa. My boss said, "Tarun, your smile is your uniform." So I smiled. Every guest, every complaint, every night shift. Broad, open, teeth showing. Guests loved it. But inside I was falling apart: my father was sick back in Belgaum, and I couldn't take leave. One night a regular guest, an old professor, looked at me and said, "Young man, that smile is working harder than you are." I nearly cried at the desk. He sat me down in the lobby and made me tell him everything. Next morning I asked my boss for three days' leave, and he gave it. A smile that comes from goodwill helps people, Noor. A smile that hides everything eats you up. Keep one person you can tell the truth to.

qa.q: Where did young Tarun work as duty manager?
qa.a: At a big hotel in Goa.

qa.q: How did young Tarun feel behind his broad smile?
qa.a: He was falling apart inside with worry about his sick father and unable to take leave.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed things for Tarun?
qa.a: The old professor noticed the strained smile, made him talk, and the next morning Tarun asked for leave and got it.

qa.q: How did the old professor see Tarun's smile?
qa.a: He saw that it was working harder than Tarun, hiding real distress.

grounding: Shows a young professional using a broad smile as a customer tool while habitual smiling over worry wears him down.

passage:
Hrithik had eleven minutes before the clients from Pune walked in, and the demo server had crashed twice that morning. Tushar was still restarting it, sweat on his forehead.
When the door opened, Hrithik's face changed: a wide, open-mouthed smile, a warm "Welcome, welcome, did you find parking?" The two visitors relaxed into their chairs. One of them even joked about the traffic.
The smile helped because Hrithik genuinely liked these clients; they had been patient for months. But halfway through, when the screen froze again, he kept grinning and saying "Small hiccup!" while his foot bounced under the table.
Afterwards, in the corridor, Tushar said quietly, "You looked like you were having fun."
"I wasn't," Hrithik admitted, rubbing his cheeks. "I've been smiling over this bug for three weeks. I'm tired, yaar."

qa.q: How many minutes did Hrithik have before the clients walked in?
qa.a: Hrithik had eleven minutes before the clients from Pune walked in.

qa.q: What does Hrithik's bouncing foot suggest while he kept grinning?
qa.a: It suggests Hrithik was anxious about the frozen screen even though his face looked cheerful; it could also have been leftover restless energy from the morning's rush.

qa.q: What could Hrithik try when a bug has worried him for weeks?
qa.a: He could tell his team lead about the strain early and share the worry with Tushar before meetings, so the smile isn't covering everything alone.

qa.q: How did the welcome affect the visiting clients?
qa.a: The clients relaxed into their chairs and joked about traffic, so the warm smile put them at ease even while the demo struggled.

grounding: A broad smile sets clients at ease when it matches real goodwill, but smiling over weeks of worry wears the person down.
